texts: On day 575 of Year 2, the cliff-spires were clearly visible from Aelmere in the morning.
Keepers walked to the base of the cliff.
The keepers counted the sky-cats on each cliff-spire.
The census of Year 1 had estimated twelve sky-cats.
The Council logged the census as an estimate.

sentences: On day 575 of Year 2, the cliff-spires were clearly visible from Aelmere in the morning.
Keepers walked to the base of the cliff.
The keepers counted the sky-cats on each cliff-spire.
The census of Year 1 had estimated twelve sky-cats.
The Council logged the census as an estimate.
parse: (: spires_vis_state (Implication (PartOf $x sk_cliff_spire_1) (And (Member (sk_visible $x) visible) (Experiencer (sk_visible $x) $x) (Source (sk_visible $x) aelmere) (Time (sk_visible $x) (Day 575)) (Time (sk_visible $x) (Year 2)) (Time (sk_visible $x) morning) (Degree (sk_visible $x) visible clearly) (Past (sk_visible $x)))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

q1_issues.issue: (Degree (sk_visible $x) visible clearly) puts the reified state in Degree's bearer slot; the bearer is the entity ($x, the spire), as in (Degree alice tall very) and the approximator's (Degree <bearer> <adjective> almost).

The past perfect "had estimated" emits Past but no ordering atom, although the text supplies later asserted events (the keepers' counting) for it to precede — the test is another asserted event in the text, not the connective.

"logged the census as an estimate" is flattened to a top-level (Member sk_census_1 estimate), asserting the classification as fact and leaving it unlinked to the logging event (no reified state, no Result, no attribution to the Council).

q2_gaps: "V X as Y" classification / predicative complement ("logged the census as an estimate", classify / record / regard X as Y): sealing is finite-clause-only, the impersonal-attitude route covers only passive "is considered to be", and the resultative shape does not fit a verb that records rather than changes its object — so nothing licensed attributes the classification to the logging.

A count that arrives as a measurement verb's numeral object under a non-veridical verb ("the census had estimated twelve sky-cats"): the entity-object route asserts a real 12-member group with (Cardinality 12) at top level, and there is no carrier marking the figure as estimated rather than actual — the passage's whole point is the 14-vs-12 contrast.
review.notes: Otherwise doctrine-clean: the plural copular distributes as a per-member reified-state rule plus the flat rule, "each cliff-spire" ranges over PartOf with its QuantifierPhrase companion, "on the cliff-spire" keeps the entity-attached On, and "the Council" correctly takes no Name atom. The instruction set leaves unclear whether a bare-plural episodic group subject with a distributive predicate ("Keepers walked to the base") must also carry the per-member rule this parse omits.

issues.reason: Degree's first slot is the BEARER entity and stays so even when the state is reified — the approximator rule spells it out, '(Degree <bearer> <adjective> almost)' beside a reified state, as does '(Degree alice tall very)' — so '(Degree (sk_visible $x) visible clearly)' predicates the degree of the state witness instead of the spire, and says nothing about how visible the spire was.

Time: 'emit the ordering whenever the sentence contains another asserted event for the perfect to precede, whatever links them', the no-ordering carve-out being reserved for 'a past perfect with no other event in the text' — this passage asserts the keepers' count (and the walking and the logging), so '(Before sk_estimate_1 sk_count_1)' is owed and its absence drops the anteriority the perfect states.

The over-assertion half stands — 'logged X as an estimate' states the Council's record of a classification, and a bare top-level '(Member sk_census_1 estimate)' launders an attributed classification into a world fact, the bar the impersonal-attitude rule states as 'the opinion is not a fact'; the half that falls is the demand for a reified state / Result / attribution link, since the instruction set licenses none (the reviewer's own gap) and Result would misencode a verb that records rather than changes its object.

gaps_confirmed: 'V X as Y' classification / predicative complement (log / record / classify / regard X as Y): nothing attributes the classification to the recording act — sealing is finite-clause-only, the impersonal-attitude route covers only passive 'is considered to be', and the resultative Result link misdescribes a verb that leaves its object unchanged.

A numeral object under a non-veridical measurement verb ('the census had estimated twelve sky-cats'): the mandated indefinite-argument route (group + Cardinality) asserts a real 12-member sky-cat group at top level, and no carrier marks the figure as an estimate rather than an actual set — which is exactly the passage's 14-vs-12 point.
new_gaps: A bare-plural episodic group subject with a distributive predicate ('Keepers walked to the base of the cliff'): the distribution doctrine names 'a grouped / counted plural', but every example it gives is definite ('the dogs barked') or counted ('both dogs barked'), so whether a bare-plural episodic group witness also owes the per-member rule is unsettled — this parse emits the per-member rule for the copular visible-state and for the per-spire counting, but not for the walking.
adjudication.defect_summary: Degree: the compliant form is '(Degree $x visible clearly)' with the spire in the bearer slot, beside the reified '(Member (sk_visible $x) visible)' state and its Experiencer. Past perfect: add the ordering atom '(Before sk_estimate_1 sk_count_1)' alongside the Past already emitted. 'Logged the census as an estimate': the instruction set licenses NO form that attributes a classification to a recording verb, so the compliant parse is the log event alone (Agent Council, Theme census, Past) with the 'as an estimate' complement left out and the gap recorded — per Core patterns, an unencodable qualifier never becomes an unqualified assertion.
adjudication.notes: The 'visible from Aelmere' vantage PP as '(Source (sk_visible $x) aelmere)' on the state witness is a defensible named-role reading and I would refute it if filed. Otherwise the parse is doctrine-clean, including the distributive reified-state-plus-flat-rule pair and the per-spire dependent Skolem groups with their QuantifierPhrase companion.
